newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai to spend five trln won in R&D.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai to spend five trln won in R&D.

text.p: Hyundai Motor Co Ltd, South Korea's largest carmaker, said on Thursday it planned to invest five trillion won for research and development over the next four years.
Hyundai spokesman Park Chang-keun said Hyundai Motor also planned to increase the number of researchers to 10,000 by 2000 from the current 6,400.
Park quoted Hyundai Motor chairman Chung Mong-gyu as saying that the move was aimed at making Hyundai Motor one of the world's top automakers in terms of production and technology.
Hyundai Motor opened an integrated research and development centre in Namyang, south of Seoul, on Wednesday, Park said.
The 350 billion won centre has designing, egineering and other R&D facilities as well as a test run ground.
